findings.title: raw_html cook method renders feed/imported HTML without any sanitization, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: The new `cook` short-circuit returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the entire rendering/sanitization pipeline. This content originates from external sources: `Jobs::PollFeed` stores RSS/Atom item bodies (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) directly, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` stores Readability output. Nothing sanitizes it, and it is rendered raw in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`) and in the normal topic UI. A malicious or compromised feed/article can therefore inject `<script>` or event-handler attributes that execute for every forum reader (stored XSS). The imported HTML should be run through the sanitizer (with an appropriate tag/attribute whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL, which browsers reject, so iframe resizing never works
findings.body: The layout calls `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The targetOrigin argument to postMessage must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]) or '*'; passing a full URL with a path (e.g. `http://blog.example.com/2013/02/10/post.html`, which is what the referer will always be) causes the browser to throw a SyntaxError ('Invalid target origin') and the message is never delivered. Since embed.js only sets the iframe height when it receives this message, the embedded comments iframe stays at the browser default height (~150px) and the comments appear cut off. The origin should be derived from the referer (or `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), not the full referer URL.

findings.title: i.content can be nil for feeds without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS only populates `content` when the feed includes `content:encoded`; many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description`, and some Atom entries lack content entirely. For those items `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, which aborts `rss.items.each` and kills the whole polling job (which has `retry: false`), so no topics are imported at all. Fall back to `i.description` or skip items with no content.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends the 'Imported from' footer directly to the string object passed in by the caller. If the same string object is ever reused (e.g. a caller importing twice with one buffer, or passing a frozen string), the footer is appended multiple times — which also changes the computed content_sha1 and triggers spurious post revisions — or raises a RuntimeError on frozen strings. Use `contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup` before appending.

findings.title: setnx followed by expire is not atomic; a crash leaves the throttle key with no TTL
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process dies (or redis errors) between the two, the key is set with no expiry, and that embed URL is treated as 'retrieved recently' forever — `perform_retrieve` will never run for it again, so the topic for that URL is never imported. Use a single atomic command such as `$redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

findings.title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters with no model-level length validation
findings.body: The migration creates `t.string :embed_url, null: false` (255-char limit) with a unique index, while `TopicEmbed` only validates presence. Blog/feed URLs frequently exceed 255 characters (tracking parameters, long slugs). For such URLs, `TopicEmbed.create!` raises a database error (or RecordNotUnique-style failure) instead of a clean validation, and `EmbedController` will keep enqueueing retrieval jobs for a URL that can never be stored. Either use `text`/a larger limit or add a length validation and gracefully skip over-long URLs.

findings.title: absolutize_urls raises URI::InvalidURIError for feed URLs that pass the loose scheme check
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` accepts any URL matching `/^https?\:\/\//`, but `absolutize_urls` then calls `URI(url)`, which raises `URI::InvalidURIError` for strings with spaces, quotes, or other invalid characters that still match the prefix regex (feed-provided `link` values in `Jobs::PollFeed` are not otherwise validated). The exception is unrescued here, so one malformed feed item aborts the entire hourly `PollFeed` run (which has `retry: false`), preventing all other items from being imported. Validate with `URI.parse` up front and skip items that fail to parse.
